references.text: Jesus decided to go to Jerusalem. [ref:Luk 9:51|Luke 9:51] marks the beginning of Jesus' journey toward Jerusalem, which is the same journey that continues in Luke 13:22. The expression "πορείαν ποιούμενος εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα" in 13:22 points back to this decisive decision.

Jesus continued his journey toward Jerusalem through cities and villages. [ref:Luk 17:11|Luke 17:11] again mentions that Jesus was on his way to Jerusalem, showing that the travel motif is a central structural framework in the Gospel of Luke.
In [ref:Luk 19:11|Luke 19:11], Jesus is near Jerusalem, marking the conclusion of the long journey mentioned in 13:22. Throughout this section, Luke emphasizes that Jerusalem is the ultimate goal.

Shortly after, in [ref:Luk 13:33|Luke 13:33], Jesus says that a prophet cannot die outside Jerusalem. This underscores the significance of his journey there – Jerusalem is the place of a prophet's destiny.
In [ref:Mark 6:6|Mark 6:6], Jesus travels around the villages and teaches. The expression "κατὰ πόλεις καὶ κώμας διδάσκων" in Luke 13:22 reflects this traveling teaching activity.
[ref:Matt 9:35|Matthew 9:35] describes how Jesus went to all the cities and villages, teaching. This is a parallel to the traveling teaching of Jesus mentioned in Luke 13:22.

In [ref:Luk 4:43-44|Luke 4:43-44], Jesus says that he must preach the kingdom of God also in other cities, for that is why he was sent. This provides the basis for the traveling preaching described in 13:22.

[ref:Luk 8:1|Luke 8:1] tells how Jesus went from city to city and from village to village, proclaiming the good news of the kingdom of God. The word pair "πόλεις καὶ κώμας" is found again in 13:22, showing that this was Jesus' regular practice.
